note: Design round 8, feature identity (Who, where and when you are away), the options chosen: user-grey for the name, both op-tag and op-name for the operator (hud.op tag and gold), and bed-blocks for the idle bed. rows are copied from the design's identity.json, verbatim but for the sample names (SOURCES.json) (each row is the full HUD of base.cjs: hud4.js MIX.render on hud4-states.json normal, fable-off, colour style, left-aligned, with the 0.6.0 frame; line 3's folder or hotbar slot 4 redrawn by the option). situations are the design's inputs (build.cjs): state is what replaces fields of states.normal (the idle one: the cache cold), who the name, host and operator look drawn (the design's USER steve, HOST DESKTOP; op tag or gold while elevated), idle whether 5 minutes passed without a message.
title: Who, where and when you are away
intro: Three small additions: your name before the folder on line 3, an operator tag when Claude Code runs as Administrator, and a bed in the empty hotbar slot 4 when you have been away for 5 minutes.

options.name: Your name in the folder's grey
options.optionNote: Line 3 ends with who you are, then the folder: "⌂ steve: D:/webapp". It reads like a Minecraft chat line, all in the same quiet grey as the folder today. User@host adds the computer name, for when you work on more than one PC.

options.name: A red [OP] before your name
options.optionNote: When Claude Code runs as Administrator, a bold red [OP] appears just before your name, like a rank on a Minecraft server chat: "[OP] steve: D:/webapp". When it runs normally there is no tag. With the name turned off it reads "⌂ [OP] D:/webapp".

options.name: Your name turns gold
options.optionNote: No extra text: when Claude Code runs as Administrator your name turns bold gold, the colour Minecraft servers often give to operators; normally it is grey. It takes no extra room, but you have to know what gold means. With the name turned off the ⌂ turns gold.

options.name: A block bed in slot 4 (plain style)
options.optionNote: The same idle bed, built from block shapes like the gold and the grass: a white pillow and a red blanket on top, oak legs at both ends. Windows Terminal draws these shapes itself in our colours, so it looks the same in colour and plain style.
